Twenty Second Indian Expedition to Antarctica, Scientific Report, 2008 
Ministry of Earth Sciences, Technical Publication No. 20, pp 243-260 
Environmental Status at Indian Antarctic 
Station Maitri 
Prashant Bhave and Medha Dixit 
Veeramata Jeejabai Technological Institute 
H.R.Mahajani Road, Matunga, Mumbai-400019 
INTRODUCTION 
Monitoring and analysis of water from Priydarshini Lake, at Indian 
Antarctic Station - Maitri, which is a source of drinking water for Maitri. 
Performance evaluation of wastewater treatment plant: Based on the 
analysis of influent and effluent, performance of the treatment plant may be 
evaluated. This will confirm whether the effluent quality is within the 
permissible limit set by the pollution regulatory authorities. 
SCOPE OF STUDY DURING XXII IAE 
Period of study: Summer expedition January 2003 to March 2003 
• Monitoring of water source to Maitri (Lake waters) and surface 
waters feeding to lakes (Tributaries) 
• Analysis of lake waters 
• Analysis of waste water generated at Maitri 
• Performance evaluation of treatment plant 
WORK PLAN DURING XXII IAE 
• Setting up of Laboratory 
• Data collection 
• Collection and analysis of samples 
• Inferences regarding lake water quality 
• Performance evaluation of treatment plant 
244 Prashant Bhave and Medha Dixit 
To carry out the performance study a temporary laboratory was set up 
at Aravali summer hut, Maitri Station. V.J.T.I. Matunga, Mumbai 400019, 
gave equipment and chemicals required for experimentation. 
Following sequence of works were undertaken during XXII IAE. 
• Monitoring program of Priydarshini lake water as well as 
some other surface waters as control waters for the quality 
comparisons 
• Performance evaluation of the wastewater treatment facilities 
at Maitri 
• Monitoring of noise levels at various locations in and around 
station. 
• Study about the solid waste management 
• Study of the Soil samples collected from the adjacent areas to 
Maitri. 
WATER 
i) Fresh Water 
Priydarshini lake is a source of water for the Maitri station from its 
inception. It's more than a decade that the water is used for all the puiposes 
at Maitri. Water samples were drawn from all around the Priydarshini lake 
and from the various locations from the middle of the lake. Water 
samples were also drawn from glaciers and a lake about 25 Km from 
the Maitri station. These samples were taken and analyzed from the 
point of view of control samples for comparisons. A few water 
samples were also analyzed at the Institute's laboratory to have inter 
laboratory studies and to have better control over the quality of analysis 
of samples. 
Water samples were collected from 26 various locations (Ref. Table 
1). The samples were characterized for various parameters as physical, 
chemical and biological. These included few field parameters as pH, 
temperature, conductivity, turbidity and dissolved oxygen (D.O), chloride, 
sulphate, bacterial contamination and a few heavy metals.

ii) Wastewater 
The wastewater is generated at Maitri station from various day-to­
day activities of the occupants from kitchen, bathroom, washrooms and 
urinals. This wastewater is disposed in to the Priydarshini lake after the 
246 Prashant Bhave and Medha Dixit 
treatment at the Maitri station. The treatment provided to the wastewater is 
mainly by passing through the bio-discs (Two in number, separately provided 
for two wastewater streams (i) Kitchen and (ii) Bathrooms & Urinals). 
Later on the effluent of the bio discs is collected in a open pond for minimum 
3 weeks in summers (December to February). The wastewater after passing 
through pond reaches ultimately to the Priydarshini lake. 
The composite samples were collected from various locations and at 
various times for the analysis. Total of 13 samples were analyzed for 
characterization. Table
